definition: PRP: thermal model fit to first mapping year (Paige 2010) on a Kaguya-DEM triangle mesh. PCP: mean bolometric brightness temperature per 240 m bin, 24 subsolar-longitude bins x 6 Ls bins (south polar release 2022). Annual mean from PCP = our own average over all bins (not published as a product that I opened).
pixel_size: PRP mesh edge about 500 m (Paige 2010 supplement); PCP 240 m
comparability_to_earth: PARTIAL: both are annual mean surface temperature in K but Moon is a topography-and-grazing-light regime and PCP is a brightness temperature not a skin temperature

product_or_paper: No Diviner product gives a polar day-night swing. Only option: our own max minus min of PCP TBOL over the 24 subsolar-longitude bins at fixed Ls.
quoted_evidence: Sun never rises above about 1.5 deg here (Williams 2019 abstract: 1.54 deg tilt; targets.yaml). The subsolar-longitude cycle is a 29.5 day shadowing cycle set by topography, not a 24 h day-night cycle.
definition: Would be DERIVED only after someone processes the PCP tables. Not done here.
comparability_to_earth: NOT COMPARABLE: Earth column is a 24 h day-night LST difference in the dry season; a polar topographic shadow cycle is a different physical quantity
